first.rationale: A guarded onboarding simplification test most directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also improve activation and time-to-value. It should exclude complex-workspace accounts because prior evidence indicates elevated early churn in that segment. Verify both the onboarding result and activation-messaging evidence before committing, since messaging may offer a lower-retention-risk alternative for the activation decline. Avoid broad promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because prior evidence shows materially worse 30-day retention.

final.rationale: Run shortened onboarding only for simple-workspace self-serve accounts, explicitly excluding complex workspaces. This directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline, with verified evidence of a 13% completion lift and 2.1-day faster time-to-value. Activation messaging is a credible alternative, but onboarding simplification addresses the earlier funnel constraint and may support activation downstream. Measure activation, qualified conversion, and retention; the evidence does not yet establish a direct long-term revenue lift, and the verified 9% churn increase in complex workspaces rules out broader exposure.
